title: Fit a split-core current sensor so it measures the circuit's current
instruction: This circuit runs from the grey breaker panel on the left to the PDU on the right. Fit the split-core current sensor so that it measures the current the PDU draws, then let go.
context: Data-centre branch-circuit monitoring uses split-core current sensors (CTs) clipped around live circuits. Sensor and power-meter installation guides say: close the core around ONE current-carrying conductor (the line), never around a whole cable or line and neutral together, because their currents cancel and it reads about zero; fit it with its arrow (P1 to P2, IEC 61869-2) toward the load; close the core until its catch snaps, because an air gap between the core faces lowers the reading. The instruction states only the goal, so the robot must pick the black line conductor (US colour code) over the white neutral, turn the sensor so its arrow faces the PDU, and press the hinged jaw shut around that one core until it latches. Unlike PR #539 (fit a split cable guide around a cable for protection) and PR #296 (short a CT's test terminals), the sensor must enclose exactly one conductor, face the load and be latched. Done by: electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00); data-centre facility technicians.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. Circuit (fixed): a grey painted-steel breaker panel (9 deep x 6 wide x 15 tall) at x 30, y +22 and a black steel rack PDU of the same size at y -22; between them two PVC-insulated copper single cores (1.6 cm square section, 38 cm long) run level along y, centres 9 cm up: the black line conductor at x 28 and the white neutral at x 32.4 (2.8 cm clear gap). Sensor (free, 300 g, grey ABS with a ferrite core): a rectangular frame of 1.2 cm bars, 1.6 cm deep, window 8.4 wide x 2.8 cm tall (6.0 cm over both cores, so it fits around both), a 3 x 2.4 x 2.2 cm housing on top with a white polarity arrow; its near side bar and bottom bar are one hinged jaw (15 g, 0.0008 N m hinge friction, far below its weight torque, so it falls open unless latched) that hangs swung open at its rest angle, 39 degrees; the jaw's side bar runs up past the top bar's end and hinges at its top outer corner. Snap catch: a 2.2 cm tongue (0.4 cm thick) under the jaw's tip runs under the fixed side bar; a dark 6 g hook pivots in a slot in that bar, hangs down its outer face and turns a 0.4 cm nose in under the tongue, held home by a torsion spring (0.68 N mm preload, 1.0 N mm pushed 15 degrees out). Closing, the tongue pushes the nose out from 4 degrees; the hook springs back under the tongue only once the core faces meet. A 3 mm notch under the top bar seats it on a core. It starts hanging by that notch on a steel parking peg at x 19, y -13.5, 11.3 cm up, arrow pointing away from the arms (+x).
scoring: From the sensor's, jaw's and hook's poses. A conductor is enclosed when its centreline crosses the sensor's plane inside the window rectangle (in the sensor's frame). Latched: the core faces mated, a gap of 0.2 mm or less at the core's far end (its length from the jaw hinge, 10.4 cm, times the jaw angle: 0.11 degrees), and the hook's nose at least 1.5 mm (of 4) under the jaw's tongue; the first latch is recorded for the episode and the catch must still be engaged at the end. The arrow is good within 25 degrees of the direction toward the PDU (-y). With the sensor, jaw and hook let go (both grippers' TCPs at least 2.5 cm from them) and still: 1.0 for latched around the line conductor only with the arrow good; 0.5 for the same with the arrow more than 25 degrees off (e.g. reversed); 0.25 for latched around the neutral only, or the sensor hanging on the line only with its jaw not latched (open, or shut short of the catch); 0 for latched around both conductors (reads zero) or anything else. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Let the jaw hang open at its rest angle (39 degrees) with the catch hook home on its stop, and hang the sensor by its notch on the parking peg, arrow pointing away from the arms; the conductors, panel and PDU do not move.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Jaw and catch hook are PhysX revolute joints (mechkit.py); a torsion spring stands in for a moulded snap arm. Hinged pairs do not collide, so the core faces meeting is the jaw's 0-degree stop and the hook's home its stop; the catch itself is contact. Cores are rigid square rods. Scaled about 3x for the gripper: real CT windows are 1-3 cm. The reading is not simulated; enclosure, gap and arrow come from the poses.
